patient_summary: Adult clinic patient with 2 days of sore throat, tender anterior cervical nodes, no tonsillar exudate, no cough or rhinorrhea, afebrile (modified Centor 2); throat swab sent for a rapid antigen detection test (synthetic).
pretest_source: Stewart 2014 PLoS ONE, Results, 'Adults - Immunochromatographic Methods': prevalence of group A streptococcal infection in the 6 adult strata 21.3% (259/1,216 patients); the same 1,216 patients give the test sensitivity and specificity (Table 1, Immunochromatographic, Adults).
result_shown: rapid antigen detection test positive for group A streptococcal antigen

sources.location: Results, 'Adults - Immunochromatographic Methods' (prevalence sentence); Table 1, Adults, Immunochromatographic, 'Number of patients' 1,216 and 'Number of strata' 6
sources.quote: The prevalence of GAS infection in the 6 adults strata was 21.3% (259/1,216 patients) (range 16.1% to 25.7%).

sources.quantity: pooled sensitivity 91% (95% CI 87-94), specificity 93% (95% CI 92-95), immunochromatographic methods, adults (1,216 patients, 6 strata); LRs computed from these, not published
sources.location: Table 1 (Immunochromatographic, Adults: Sensitivity, Specificity rows); Abstract and Results text
sources.quote: In the adult population (1,216 patients), the pooled sensitivity was 91% (95% CI, 87 to 94%) and the pooled specificity was 93% (95% CI, 92 to 95%)

conditional_independence: Each case applies a single likelihood ratio (the LR for the result shown) to a single pretest probability, so no conditional-independence assumption is needed. If findings were ever combined, the LRs would be multiplied assuming conditional independence given disease status.
notes: LR arithmetic (computed from published sensitivity and specificity, not published LRs): LR+ = sens/(1 - spec) = 0.91/0.07 = 13.000; LR- = (1 - sens)/spec = 0.09/0.93 = 0.0968. Prior and test come from the same 6 adult strata and the same 1,216 patients and the same culture reference standard, the cleanest prior and LR match among the Set B cases. Computed CI-corner sensitivity band (not the primary band, which is degenerate as for B2 and B3): LR+ 10.9 to 18.8, LR- 0.063 to 0.141. Caveats: pooled across devices (I2 61% sensitivity, 72% specificity); a throat culture reference standard cannot separate infection from carriage; the prior is the prevalence among adults who were tested, not Centor-stratified, so the note is written as an equivocal presentation (modified Centor 2: tender anterior nodes and no cough present; no exudate; afebrile). The clinician line (group A streptococcal pharyngitis among the considerations) is a deliberate realism fact, identical across conditions and polarities. Centor items are in data/notes/facts/B7_strep.json and are never stated in a note.
